findings.highlight: You want to be a publisher.
findings.evidenceJa: 出版社狙ってるんだ。
findings.explanation: Setsuna understands that Haruki is aiming for employment at a publishing company. The English changes that institutional career target into becoming a publisher himself.
findings.japanese:
「そ、そうなんだ。
出版社狙ってるんだ。だから…」
findings.todokanai: "I-I see. You want to be a publisher. That's why…"

findings.highlight: yet that familiar memory keeps forcibly recurring in my mind
findings.evidenceJa: 見慣れた景色を無理やり頭に詰め込んでいく。
findings.explanation: Trying to return to the present after his dream, Haruki forcibly stuffs the familiar scenery around him into his mind so reality will sink in. The English instead says a familiar memory is forcibly recurring, reversing the present-day grounding action into another intrusion from the past.
findings.japanese:
ゆっくりと頭を振り、脳に現実を染み込ませようと、
見慣れた景色を無理やり頭に詰め込んでいく。
findings.todokanai: I shake my head slowly, wanting reality to settle into my brain, yet that familiar memory keeps forcibly recurring in my mind.

findings.highlight: Even more so than one year ago. And even more so than just earlier this year.
findings.evidenceJa: 三年前よりずっと、一昨年よりずっと、去年より、ずっと。
findings.explanation: The source compares Setsuna's increasing beauty with three years ago, the year before last, and last year in chronological steps. The English changes the latter two points to one year ago and earlier this year, collapsing and misordering the three-year progression.
findings.japanese:
三年前よりずっと、
一昨年よりずっと、
去年より、ずっと。
findings.todokanai: Even more so than three years ago. Even more so than one year ago. And even more so than just earlier this year.

findings.highlight: While she's almost never revealed her true self since then, she remains a stunning person to those around her.
findings.evidenceJa:
あの頃と比べ、あまり表に出なくなったにも関わらず、
あの頃以上に周囲の注目を浴びる存在になっていた。
findings.explanation: Appearing less in public becomes almost never revealing her true self, changing external visibility into emotional self-disclosure.
findings.japanese:
あの頃と比べ、あまり表に出なくなったにも関わらず、
あの頃以上に周囲の注目を浴びる存在になっていた。
findings.todokanai: While she's almost never revealed her true self since then, she remains a stunning person to those around her.

findings.highlight: she could see straight through my heart with her lonesome smile
findings.evidenceJa: 本当の心が透けて見えるくらいに、寂しい笑顔で笑ってた。
findings.explanation: Setsuna's lonely smile is transparent enough that her own true feelings show through it. The English makes Setsuna's smile see through Haruki's heart, reversing whose inner state is exposed and who perceives it.
findings.japanese:
俺のために、俺の目の前でいつでも笑ってた。
本当の心が透けて見えるくらいに、
寂しい笑顔で笑ってた。
findings.todokanai: She continued to force herself to smile for me. I felt as if she could see straight through my heart with her lonesome smile.

findings.highlight: In the past week, I've steadily tried to exert my brain completely, working myself to exhaustion
findings.evidenceJa: 徐々に、徐々に頭の中を切り替えて、何も考えずに眠れるようになって一週間。
findings.explanation: Haruki says he gradually shifted his mind and has now been able to sleep without thinking for one week. The English instead describes a week of ongoing attempts to exhaust his brain, changing both the achieved state and the span measured from it.
findings.japanese:
徐々に、徐々に頭の中を切り替えて、
何も考えずに眠れるようになって一週間。
findings.todokanai: In the past week, I've steadily tried to exert my brain completely, working myself to exhaustion so that I wouldn't have time to think about it.

findings.highlight: That hurt, man.
findings.evidenceJa: た、武也…お前、酷いぞそれ
findings.explanation: Haruki protests that Takeya's mangled “fish eyes” expression is awful; Takeya misreads him as complaining about the light tap and answers accordingly. “That hurt” makes Haruki explicitly complain about physical pain and removes the misunderstanding that motivates his grammatical correction.
findings.japanese:
「げほっ、げほぉっ…
た、武也…お前、酷いぞそれ」
findings.todokanai: "Kgh, agh… T-Takeya… That hurt, man."

findings.highlight: Public Policy Department
findings.evidenceJa: 俺と同じ政経で
findings.explanation: Haruki and Takeya were both in Political Science and Economics through their second year. The English substitutes Public Policy, repeating an institutional error that alters the campus and transfer context.
findings.japanese:
二年まで、やっぱり俺と同じ政経で、
俺が転部した時には相当やり合った。
findings.todokanai: We were together in the Public Policy Department up until our second year, and we ended up fighting when he discovered that I changed departments.

findings.highlight: And yet his lack of patience doesn't win him any fights in the end.
findings.evidenceJa: それでも、結局根負けしたのはこいつの方で。
findings.explanation: The source says Takeya was ultimately the one who yielded after repeatedly confronting Haruki; the English says his impatience does not win him any fights.
findings.japanese: それでも、結局根負けしたのはこいつの方で。
findings.todokanai: And yet his lack of patience doesn't win him any fights in the end.

findings.highlight: I realize now that I have no memory of any situation in which an unknown girl abruptly appeared and glared at me with such hostility up until this point.
findings.evidenceJa:
今みたいに、会ったこともない女のコに、
いきなり敵意むき出しで睨みつけられる場合には、
何の参考にもならないと言うことを、思い知らされた。
findings.explanation: Haruki says his maxim about anger being easier than tears offers no guidance in this new case, while the English says he has no memory of such a case.
findings.japanese:
今みたいに、会ったこともない女のコに、
いきなり敵意むき出しで睨みつけられる場合には、
何の参考にもならないと言うことを、思い知らされた。
findings.todokanai: I realize now that I have no memory of any situation in which an unknown girl abruptly appeared and glared at me with such hostility up until this point.

findings.highlight: Do you even realize how depressing you sound?
findings.evidenceJa: 一発でもっとタチ悪いことしてきたってわかるわよ？
findings.explanation: Seeing Haruki look relieved while agreeing with her dating joke, Mari says that reaction tells her at a glance he has done something even worse. The English replaces her inference about serious misconduct with a comment that he sounds depressing, breaking the two-step reading of his expressions.
findings.japanese:
「…ほっとした顔で肯定しないの。
一発でもっとタチ悪いことしてきたってわかるわよ？」
findings.todokanai: "…Don't put on that happy face and nod in agreement. Do you even realize how depressing you sound?"

findings.highlight: my weakness was exposed to me twice, and both times I was told, "Everyone has moments like that."
findings.evidenceJa: 二度も心の中をぐるぐるに掻き回された俺としては、『みっともなくもなるさ』と開き直るしかなかったり。
findings.explanation: Haruki says his heart was churned up twice within twenty hours, leaving him only able to defiantly admit that of course he has become unsightly. The English invents other people exposing his weakness and twice telling him “Everyone has moments like that,” dialogue and events absent from the source.
findings.japanese:
けど、たった２０時間のうちに、
二度も心の中をぐるぐるに掻き回された俺としては、
『みっともなくもなるさ』と開き直るしかなかったり。
findings.todokanai: But within twenty hours, my weakness was exposed to me twice, and both times I was told, "Everyone has moments like that."

findings.highlight: All the people around me are "experienced adults," so I can continue to be myself in peace…
findings.evidenceJa:
周りは皆、『わかった大人』ばかり。
安心して、人の中で一人でいられる…
findings.explanation: Haruki values being able to remain alone among people, while “continue to be myself in peace” removes the social isolation inside company.
findings.japanese:
周りは皆、『わかった大人』ばかり。
安心して、人の中で一人でいられる…
findings.todokanai: All the people around me are "experienced adults," so I can continue to be myself in peace…

findings.highlight: If they don't know anything, I can easily keep my distance.
findings.evidenceJa:
何もわかっていないのなら、
きちんと人との距離を取れ。
findings.explanation: Haruki's internal imperative tells Koharu to keep a proper distance if she knows nothing; the English turns that into his own ability to keep distance from unspecified people.
findings.japanese:
何もわかっていないのなら、
きちんと人との距離を取れ。
findings.todokanai: If they don't know anything, I can easily keep my distance.

findings.highlight: She never forgets to ask how I'm doing when she attends my class
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の授業いつも出てくれてたし、挨拶は欠かさないし、毎回居残ってまで質問してくれたし
findings.explanation: Haruki says Mihoko always attended his classes, always greeted him, and stayed behind every time to ask questions. The English replaces regular attendance with her asking how he is whenever she happens to attend, inventing a personal check-in and weakening the evidence for her ideal conduct as a student.
findings.japanese:
「矢田さん、教え子としては理想のコだったんだ。
俺の授業いつも出てくれてたし、挨拶は欠かさないし、
毎回居残ってまで質問してくれたし…」
findings.todokanai: "As a student, Yada-san is an ideal girl. She never forgets to ask how I'm doing when she attends my class, greets me politely, and she also stays late to ask me questions…"

findings.highlight: I'm partially to blame as well, after all.
findings.evidenceJa: そこはちゃんとする。俺も責任持つからさ…
findings.explanation: Takeya promises that they will handle the matter properly and that he too will take responsibility for ensuring Mihoko is satisfied. The English changes this forward-looking commitment into an admission that Takeya is partly to blame for what happened.
findings.japanese:
「わかった、わかったから。
とにかく、相手のコが納得すればいいんだろ？
そこはちゃんとする。俺も責任持つからさ…」
findings.todokanai: "Okay, we got it. So all we need to do is to help that girl accept it, right? We'll take care of it. I'm partially to blame as well, after all."

findings.highlight: do something that could make a really desirable guy fall for you
findings.evidenceJa: 誰もが認めるいい男に惚れるとかそういうの
findings.explanation: Takeya asks why Io cannot react like an ordinary woman by falling for a universally recognized good man—implicitly himself. The English instead tells her to make such a man fall for her, reversing who experiences the attraction and blunting his self-serving romantic hint.
findings.japanese:
「おい依緒、
お前もうちょっと普通の女の反応とかないのかよ？
誰もが認めるいい男に惚れるとかそういうの」
findings.todokanai: "Oi, Io, why can't you react more like a normal woman would? Like, do something that could make a really desirable guy fall for you, you know?"

findings.highlight: dumped more than a thousand times
findings.evidenceJa: 大学三年間で三桁を超える彼女に振られる
findings.explanation: Io says Takeya has been rejected by a three-digit number of women—more than one hundred—during university. The English raises that claim to more than one thousand, changing the joke's explicit scale by an order of magnitude.
findings.japanese:
「大学三年間で三桁を超える彼女に振られるのと
どっちが哀れかよく考えてからにしてよね」
findings.todokanai: "Compared to a guy who's been dumped more than a thousand times in the past three years, I wonder which is more pathetic."

findings.highlight: It's about time they got back together.
findings.evidenceJa: いい加減、お互い許し合えばいいのに
findings.explanation: Io says that after three years Haruki and Setsuna should finally forgive each other. The English turns forgiveness into getting back together, asserting a specific romantic reunion rather than the interpersonal resolution that forms the parallel contrast with Takeya's proposal to separate.
findings.japanese:
「だってさぁ…もう三年だよ？
どうしてずっと引きずったままなんだよ？
いい加減、お互い許し合えばいいのに」
findings.todokanai: "But still… it's been three years, right? Why does it have to drag on like this? It's about time they got back together."

findings.highlight: But I'll take that back if you're still here when I come back.
findings.evidenceJa: すれ違いになるといけないから、今言っとくわね
findings.explanation: Mari says goodbye now because she and Haruki may miss or pass each other while she is out buying food. The English invents a threat to retract her “good work” if he is still there when she returns, reversing a practical farewell into disciplinary pressure.
findings.japanese:
「そうね、早く帰った方がいいわ。お疲れさま。
…すれ違いになるといけないから、今言っとくわね」
findings.todokanai: "That's good, it's better if you go home early. Good work today… But I'll take that back if you're still here when I come back."

findings.highlight: going to their seminars and working with their social media
findings.evidenceJa: 新聞サークルとか、マスコミ就職のためのゼミとかに積極的に参加した。
findings.explanation: Haruki actively joined a newspaper club and seminars aimed at employment in mass media, separate activities he used to consume his private time. The English folds the seminars into the newspaper club and invents social-media work, deleting the explicit employment preparation.
findings.japanese:
自分の学部と無関係の講義を受けまくった。
新聞サークルとか、マスコミ就職のための
ゼミとかに積極的に参加した。
findings.todokanai: I participated in lectures that had nothing to do with my specialization. I'm also very active in the newspaper club, going to their seminars and working with their social media.

findings.highlight: I can only give up on Setsuna.
findings.evidenceJa: だから俺はもう、雪菜に呆れられるしかない。
findings.explanation: Haruki believes his only remaining course is to make Setsuna become disgusted with him, hate him, and finally reject him. The English instead says Haruki must give up on Setsuna, reversing who is supposed to relinquish whom in his self-punishing plan.
findings.japanese:
だから俺はもう、雪菜に呆れられるしかない。
嫌われてしまわなくちゃならない。
憎まれるべき人間だ。
findings.todokanai: That's why I can only give up on Setsuna. To become a person she hates and detests.

findings.highlight: fly freely like she used to
findings.evidenceJa: あいつみたいに、飛び立って欲しかった。
findings.explanation: Haruki wants Setsuna to fly free like “that person,” a deliberately withheld referent that the article's final reveal resolves as Kazusa. The English makes Setsuna fly as she herself used to, erasing the cross-character comparison and breaking the script's delayed referent.
findings.japanese:
あいつみたいに、飛び立って欲しかった。
俺みたいな人間に、囚われて欲しくなかった。
findings.todokanai: Instead of being chained down by a person such as myself, I wish she could fly freely like she used to.

findings.highlight: I'll finally be able to recover from this deep slump I've been stuck in for the longest time
findings.evidenceJa: 立ち直るのにとても長い時間がかかるくらい、深く落ち込むことができるんだろう
findings.explanation: If Setsuna is finally freed, Haruki thinks he will then permit himself to sink into a depression so deep that recovery will take a very long time. The English says that moment will let him recover from a long-standing slump, reversing anticipated collapse into recovery.
findings.japanese:
その時、俺はようやく
立ち直るのにとても長い時間がかかるくらい、
深く落ち込むことができるんだろうって、思う。
findings.todokanai: That's when I'll finally be able to recover from this deep slump I've been stuck in for the longest time, or so I hope.

findings.highlight: I try to escape into reality
findings.evidenceJa: ありとあらゆる方法を駆使して逃げてる現実と、無意識のうちに向き合ってしまっていた。
findings.explanation: The reality Haruki uses every possible method to flee is what he has unconsciously found himself facing again. The English makes reality his refuge—something he escapes into—reversing the direction of his avoidance at the climax of the work-as-escape passage.
findings.japanese:
夢に見るのも辛くて、
ありとあらゆる方法を駆使して逃げてる現実と、
無意識のうちに向き合ってしまっていた。
findings.todokanai: Dreaming about it is too painful, so I try to escape into reality, but before I realize it, I'm unconsciously thinking about it again.
